newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN GRAIN HARVEST ADVANCES AMID SUNNY WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN GRAIN HARVEST ADVANCES AMID SUNNY WEATHER.

text.p: Sunny weather since Sunday has allowed speedy harvesting efforts in Germany, where farmers hope to complete the bulk of grain harvesting within the next fortnight, farm union DBV said in a harvest update.
The barley harvest was mostly complete, with yields in a range up to 10 percent above or below last year's average 5.61 tonnes per hectare (tph), it said.
Mecklenburg, Brandenburg and Saxony state, which last year had extremely bad winter barley yields, reported much improved results.
Ex-farm prices in these eastern German states were 200-220 marks a tonne, with much barley earmarked for internal on-farm feeding.
Reports from the spring barley crop pointed to an average result.
Farmers hoping their spring barley would qualify for malting purposes, which brings higher revenue, reported the desirable low protein counts were being achieved, but it was too early to generalise.
Winter wheat was being brought in in the south west but again, it was too early to assess yields and qualities.

Last year's 7.32 tph average yield was extremely high and may not be repeated but any yield falls may be offset by an area expansion in winter wheat to 2.65 million ha from 2.54 million last year, DBV said.
DBV also said about 25 percent of winter rye had been cut. Baking qualities measured in falling numbers were not satisfactory and farmgate prices were as low as 200-220 marks.
Harvesting of feed peas and triticale was also underway.
Rapeseed harvests showed satisfactory yields and good oil contents above 40 percent but moisture above nine percent meant farmers were incurring drying costs.
Rapeseed farmgate prices were around 400 marks.
National meteorological office DWD forecast maximum day temperatures between 28 and 30 degrees up to August 13 with some rainfall.
